directAnswer: Pope St. Paschal I, a Roman monk and abbot, reigned from 817 to 824. He obtained the Pactum Ludovicianum confirming papal lands, crowned Lothair I as co-emperor, and is remembered above all as a builder: Santa Prassede, Santa Cecilia in Trastevere, and Santa Maria in Domnica still display the mosaics he commissioned.

paras: Paschal, son of Bonosus and Theodora, was a Roman cleric who had led the monastery of St. Stephen near St. Peter's, which cared for pilgrims. He was elected the day after Stephen IV died and consecrated before the emperor could confirm the choice, then sent an embassy to Louis the Pious to explain.

In 817 Louis issued the Pactum Ludovicianum, a privilege confirming the territories of the Roman Church and recognizing the freedom of papal elections. In 823 Paschal crowned Louis's son Lothair as co-emperor in Rome, strengthening the custom that imperial coronation belonged to the pope.

sections.h2: The Mosaic Churches of Paschal I
paras: Paschal's most lasting legacy is visible today. He rebuilt Santa Prassede near St. Mary Major and added the Chapel of St. Zeno, its walls covered in gold-ground mosaics; one image shows his mother Theodora with a square halo, the sign of a living person, and the label episcopa. He also rebuilt Santa Maria in Domnica on the Caelian Hill, whose apse mosaic shows Paschal kneeling at the feet of the Virgin and Child.

In Trastevere he rebuilt the basilica of Santa Cecilia. The Liber Pontificalis relates that after a long search he found the body of St. Cecilia in a catacomb along the Appian Way and translated it to her church, together with the remains of companions associated with her. Paschal transferred many other martyrs' relics into Roman churches as well.

Paschal welcomed Greek monks fleeing the renewed iconoclasm of Emperor Leo V. Late in his reign two pro-Frankish officials, Theodore and Leo, were blinded and beheaded at the Lateran. Imperial envoys investigated, and Paschal swore an oath that he had not ordered the killings, while maintaining that the victims had been guilty of treason.
He died in February 824 amid local hostility; the Liber Pontificalis is silent on the details. He was nevertheless venerated as a saint in Rome, and the churches he built remain his best memorial.

keyFacts: Former abbot of the monastery of St. Stephen by St. Peter's
Received the Pactum Ludovicianum from Louis the Pious (817)
Built or rebuilt Santa Prassede, Santa Cecilia in Trastevere, and Santa Maria in Domnica
Translated the relics of St. Cecilia to her basilica

faqs.question: Where can you see Pope Paschal I's mosaics today?
faqs.answer: In Rome at Santa Prassede (including the Chapel of St. Zeno), Santa Maria in Domnica, and Santa Cecilia in Trastevere. Several of the apse mosaics show Paschal himself with the square halo of a living donor.

faqs.question: Did Paschal I find St. Cecilia's body?
faqs.answer: According to the Liber Pontificalis, he located her remains in a catacomb on the Appian Way and moved them to the rebuilt basilica of Santa Cecilia in Trastevere.

faqs.question: What was the Pactum Ludovicianum?
faqs.answer: It was a privilege issued by Emperor Louis the Pious in 817 that confirmed the lands held by the Roman Church and acknowledged the freedom of papal elections.
